summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style overview of the FA Cup, covering its broadcasting rights history, the trophy and winners' privileges, past finalists from outside the top flight, sponsorship deals, and the timing of the final. It also notes Arsenal's 2015 win and Chasetown's run to the Third Round Proper in 2007–08. The content is a mix of record-keeping on winners and finalists and the evolution of TV and radio coverage.
one_line: Overview of the FA Cup's broadcasting rights, trophy, sponsorship, notable non-top-flight winners and finalists, and final timing.
key_facts: ITV lost the FA Cup rights beginning with the 2014–15 FA Cup, and terrestrial rights returned to BBC Sport, with the final shown on BBC One.
BT Sport held the pay TV rights to the FA Cup from the 2014–15 season.
Arsenal beat Aston Villa 4–0 in the 2015 final to win the cup for the second year in a row, their 12th FA Cup title overall.
Arsenal's 12 FA Cup titles made them the competition's most successful club, ahead of Manchester United on 11.
The FA Cup trophy has had two designs and five actual cups; the latest is a 2014 replica of the second design, introduced in 1911.

Notts County (1894), Tottenham Hotspur (1901), Wolverhampton Wanderers (1908), Barnsley (1912), West Bromwich Albion (1931), Sunderland (1973), Southampton (1976) and West Ham United (1980) are the only winners who were not in the top flight.
Tottenham Hotspur were playing in the Southern League when they won in 1901 and were only elected to the Football League in 1908, making them the only non-league winners of the FA Cup.
Southampton (1902) was the last finalist from outside the top two tiers, and no finalist has come from the third tier or lower.
Since the start of the 1994–95 season, the FA Cup has been sponsored, and the sponsored name always includes 'The FA Cup'.
Emirates airline became the sponsor from 2015 to 2018, renaming the competition 'The Emirates FA Cup'.
ESPN took over the FA Cup package Setanta held from the 2010–11 season, and this rights package transferred to BT Sport from the 2013–14 season after ESPN's UK and Ireland channels were sold to BT.
The first national final on BBC Radio was between Arsenal and Cardiff in 1927, following a 1926 final broadcast only in Manchester.
The sharing of rights between BBC and ITV continued from 1955 to 1988, when ITV lost coverage to the new Sports Channel, which later became Sky Sports.
The final is normally held the Saturday after the Premier League season finishes in May.
The 2010–11 and 2012–13 finals were played before the Premier League season had finished to allow Wembley Stadium to be ready for the UEFA Champions League final.
Chasetown, playing at Level 8 of English football in the 2007–08 competition, are the lowest-ranked team to play in the Third Round Proper, out of 731 teams entered that season.
Chasetown lost to Cardiff City, the eventual FA Cup runners-up that year, and their success earned them over £60,000 in prize money.
